implantation. Neointimal healing reduces the volume of acute stent malapposition with many acute stent malapposition struts becoming completely integrated into the vessel wall. However, cases of acute stent malapposition with a large volume or acute stent malapposition located within the edges of the stent were not resolved in most cases. Thus, acute stent malapposition volume and location within stent edges were identified as independent predictors of late-persistent stent malapposition. Our results indicate that an acute stent malapposition with a larger volume or area is more likely to persist at follow-up examinations, which is consistent with findings from previous studies. 4,6,8 Late-persistent stent malapposition could be differentiated from resolved acute stent malapposition by an acute
